title: Regulatory transitions and midnight rules
summary: A change in administration creates different legal options depending on whether a rule is still internal, submitted for publication, published, or already effective.
notes:
Midnight rules are regulations completed near the end of an administration. The reading distinguishes four stages: a final draft not sent to the Federal Register; a submitted rule awaiting publication; a published rule awaiting its effective date; and an effective rule. Incoming administrations have used review freezes, withdrawal requests, and delayed effective dates, but those tools remain bounded by applicable law.

The editors emphasize litigation against efforts to delay or remove effective rules without another notice-and-comment process. A presidential preference for reconsideration does not itself supply an exception to procedural requirements governing an agency. The historical examples therefore connect political turnover to the APA’s requirements for changing policy rather than treating every rule as removable by an internal memorandum.
